'''Antonio Pizzi''' ([[Rome]], 15 May 1946)<ref>{{cite web | title=PIZZI Antonio | website=lermab.univ-lorraine.fr | url=https://lermab.univ-lorraine.fr/membres/pizzi-antonio | language=fr | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref> is an Italian-born, French-South African polymer and materials chemist, and professor emeritus of industrial chemistry at the [[University of Lorraine]], who is an expert in the field of wood adhesives<ref>{{cite web | title= IUFRO Awards| url=https://euagenda.eu/upload/publications/iufro-outstanding-science-and-services-awards.pdf | access-date=2024-12-18}} Dr. Antonio Pizzi (page 140)</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Antonio Pizzi | website=IntechOpen | date=2024-10-22 | url=https://www.intechopen.com/profiles/226217 | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref> and an elected fellow (''FIAWS'') and distinguished member of the [[International Academy of Wood Science]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Fellows | website=The International Academy of Wood Science| date=14 November 2012 | url=https://www.iaws-web.org/fellows--dues/overview-of-fellows/ | ref={{sfnref | The International Academy of Wood Science| 2012}} | access-date=18 December 2024}}</ref>

== Career ==
Pizzi holds multiple degrees, including a doctorate in chemistry (D.Chem.) from the University of Rome (1970), as well as a PhD in organic chemistry and a DSc degree in wood chemistry, both from universities in [[South Africa]]. His early career combined academic roles with industry experience, which provided a foundation for his year-long research contributions in the field.

From the period 1989 to 1995, he served as a university professor of polymer chemistry at the [[University of the Witwatersrand]] in [[Johannesburg]]. He was the head of the Department of Chemistry in the years 1991-1993. He returned to Europe in 1994. He then joined the [[University of Lorraine]] in [[France]], and initiated the Lab of Study and Research on Wood Materials (LERMAB-ENSTIB).

The research work of Pizzi focuses mostly on the polycondensation resins, including both ''green'' and synthetic wood adhesives. He is widely acknowledged for advancing the development and application of adhesives derived from renewable materials.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Scientific Achievement Award of the International Union of Forest Research Organizations|url=https://www.iufro.org/media/fileadmin/publications/general-publications/iufro-scientific-achievement-award-winners-2024.pdf|access-date=2026-09-23}} pg. 43 (A. Pizzi)</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Prof. Antonio Pizzi receives the 2022 Wake Memorial Medal|website=Tech Science Press|date=2026-09-14|url=https://www.techscience.com/ndetail/152|access-date=2026-09-23}}</ref>

== Recognition ==
Throughout his career, Pizzi has published extensively, authoring more than 1,000 research articles, patents,<ref>{{cite web | title=Patents of Dr. Antonio Pizzi | website=patents.google.com | url=https://patents.google.com/?inventor=Antonio+Pizzi&oq=Antonio+Pizzi | access-date=2024-12-18}}</ref> and over 12 books, including foundational works on bioadhesives and bioresins. His research contributions have earned international scientific awards, reflecting his influence on the field of industrial and polymer chemistry. Pizzi's work is particularly related to the areas of renewable resources and environmentally friendly adhesive technologies. Until July 2025, his research work is well recognised in the fields of [[materials science]] and [[wood science|wood science and technology]], having almost 30,000 citations at [[Scopus]],<ref>https://www.scopus.com/authid/detail.uri?authorId=7102104085 Antonio Pizzi at Scopus</ref> and more than 51,800 citations at [[Google Scholar]],<ref>{{cite web | title=A.Pizzi | website=Google Scholar | url=https://scholar.google.fr/citations?user=dl5FR3AAAAAJ&hl=fr | language=fr | access-date=2026-01-30}}</ref> with a very high [[h-index]] of 102.

In 2022,  Pizzi received the prestigious Bill Wake Memorial Medal for his yearlong research work in adhesion and adhesives.<ref>{{cite web | title= IAWS - Election of New Fellows 2022| url=https://www.iaws-web.org/downloads/Bulletin-2023_1.pdf | access-date=2025-06-11}} page 12</ref>

In October 2023, a [[metascience|meta-research]] conducted by [[John Ioannidis]] et al. at the [[Stanford University]] included Antonio Pizzi in ''Elsevier Data 2022,'' where he was ranked at the top 2% of researchers of all time in the area of materials, having a very high [[Composite index (metrics)|composite index]] of 4.0955.<ref>{{citation | last=Baas | first=Jeroen | title=October 2023 data-update for "Updated science-wide author databases of standardized citation indicators" | chapter=Bibliometrics | date=2023 | volume=6 | publisher=Elsevier Data Repository | doi=10.17632/BTCHXKTZYW.6 | url=https://data.mendeley.com/datasets/btchxktzyw/6 | access-date=2025-07-21| page= line: 12,824}}</ref>

In addition, Pizzi has won the prestigious ''Schweighofer Wood Innovation'' award in 2005,<ref>{{cite web | title=2005 Schweighofer Prize | website=Woodland Heritage | date=2008-01-31 | url=https://www.woodlandheritage.org/library-archive/2018/4/19/2005-schweighofer-prize | access-date=2025-07-21}}</ref> and also twice the ''Descartes Research Prize'', awarded by the European Commission.<ref>{{cite web | title=2005 Descartes Research Prize: nominees\nannounced | website=European Commission - European Commission | date=2005-07-12 | url=https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_05_914 | access-date=2025-07-21}}</ref>
